problem: The runner is 21 modules, 4,732 lines; launch.mjs alone is 887 and is the only writer of launch.json (new, activate, phase, gate, pin, end, land, escalate, note). The commands that write exactly one artefact from arguments are boundary, locked, budget, check, the three renders, evidence, report, plan render, runlog stub, return and events append. distribute and doctor are installation. Fifty-seven of v1's 78 behaviours name the runner.

questions.why: Fixes whether the spec has an interface node for a command program at all. A kept name keeps its shim, output library and one-line rule; scripts by path have none of those and each stands alone.

options.value: Keep fc as a thin dispatcher over leaf scripts; every leaf also runs by its own path (node flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/<leaf>.mjs) so nothing depends on the dispatcher.
Dissolve fc: leaf scripts under flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/, each invoked by path; no dispatcher, no shared name.
Keep fc as it is, including the launch subcommands, and only stop the spec from describing it.

questions.answer: custom: rename to flight; thin dispatcher; leaves autonomous; 'launch' houses flightcrew's scripts; two new commands flight launch init (scaffolds a launch with the first run stubbed) and flight launch run (new run if the previous ended); single-artefact commands may be absorbed into hooks, workflows and frontmatter

questions.text: Which built commands survive as leaves?
questions.why: Each kept leaf is a reused asset no unit rebuilds; each dropped one is retired code and retired test suites. The launch state subcommands are excluded on the problem's own terms.

options.value: check (with boundary and locked folded in as one evidence write)
the dispatch renders (worker, critic, verifier, plus a new explorer and planner render)
evidence page, report and run-log stub
plan render (plan.md from plan.json)
return (schema-validated store of a role's return)
validate and lint (already leaves; unchanged)
budget
worker merge
distribute and doctor (installation)

questions.answer: the dispatch renders (worker, critic, verifier, plus explorer and planner); heavy investigation via explorers; plan stays JSON only

questions.text: Which new leaves does the layout need, since nothing today creates a launch folder or a numbered run?
questions.why: A launch and a run are now folders with a defined file set. Something must scaffold them, and whether that is a script or a copied template decides whether the interval before a spec exists is modelled.

options.value: Two leaves: one opens launch/<name>/ from an idea (specs/, interview/, a draft spec from the template) and one opens runs/run-<n>/ under it.
One leaf that opens the launch; a run folder is created by the workflow that starts the run.
No new leaf: templates are copied by hand or by the role that needs the folder.

questions.answer: answered in Q1: two scaffolds under flight launch

questions.text: Is this the spec seam for v2: a node about an artefact's state, a hook's enforcement, a role's inputs and outputs or a rendering's contents stays; a node about arguments, resolution order, exit codes or which subcommand does what leaves?
questions.why: This is the rule I will retire v1 nodes by. Roughly forty behaviours and edges fall to it. What survives of the runner is one constraint on leaf scripts (exit codes, one-line success output, its named exceptions) and the artefacts they write.

options.value: Yes, that seam, with one constraint node for leaf scripts.
That seam, but keep a short interface node listing the leaf names and the artefact each writes.
Narrower: retire only the launch-state nodes; keep the leaf commands' argument shapes in interfaces.

questions.answer: custom: each node judged individually keep/change/remove, by what the following agents need

questions.text: The four manuals written as command sequences (launch-anatomy, journey, workflows, review): in this run?
questions.why: Manuals are context an agent cannot test. Rewriting them to the seam is a unit of work; leaving them is a false premise handed to every role that reads them.

options.value: In scope: rewritten to describe artefacts, roles and gates; no command in them.
In scope, but only the launch README and anatomy; the rest deleted and their content folded into role files.
Out of scope: a later run.

questions.answer: (unanswered) — taken from the problem text: the four manuals are rewritten to the seam
